BLOCK exact candidate 2f033f11a2efa718e2cd05de98c0ef3154ea024d.

The committed court passes, and the author receipt hash matches bf9e1f232faf6ee1633c7c9d6384874c5329704f284f89c33265945114d322a7. The named pending, abandoned, superseded, unknown, missing-phase, duplicate-OID, candidate-show failure/contradiction/malformed, and candidate-list command/malformed-JSON cases behave fail-closed.

One malformed typed-row case remains fail-open. In step 7 the parser assigns:
  candidate_id = r.get("candidate_id") or r.get("id") or "<missing>"
It then accepts that sentinel as a valid single-line string. In an exact-candidate export I extended the court with:
  [{"identity":{"commit_oid":"<the first-parent bypass oid>"},"phase":{"value":"landed"}}]
with candidate_id omitted. The checker exited 0 and printed:
  reconciled first-parent candidate: 55970ed <missing> (landed)
  Mechanical checks passed.

That row is not a candidate identity or a valid landing receipt, but it exempts the first-parent commit. This contradicts the requested malformed-state fail-closed contract.

Required successor: reject every enumerated row with a commit OID unless candidate_id is a nonempty typed identity and phase is a typed value; do not replace missing identity fields with display sentinels. Add exact-exit-3 courts for missing and empty candidate ids, plus a malformed row beside an otherwise valid row so malformed entries cannot be silently ignored. Preserve the existing unique landed/landed_out_of_band exemption and all current negative courts.

No candidate source was edited. The adversarial test existed only in /private/tmp/storymodel4s-premerge-review.bfpG2W.
